layout_dets.text: 5.1.4. Context Access

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The coeffect operations of Section 5.1.2 form a reflective API: a coeffect is written with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ctx. set(key, value) and read with ctx. get (key), both keyed by name. Cordis layers a second,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an access to a coeffect, atop the primitive get of Section 5.1.2.

layout_dets.text: 5.2. Component Loader

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The core library equips component developers with imperative primitives for dynamic compo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sition, such as ctx.effect, ctx.use, and ctx.set. A separate concern arises for application

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: orchestrators, who assemble pre-existing components into a running system and adjust the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition over its lifetime. The component loader addresses this concern by introducing a de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clarative configuration layer: the orchestrator specifies the desired composition as a persistent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data structure, and the loader translates changes to this specification into the corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imperative fiber operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.2.1. Declarative Configuration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 4 decomposes a running system into fibers, each an instantiation of one component.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Everything an instantiation needs can be declared, so an orchestrator can describe a whole

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system as a declarative configuration: a persistent record that the loader realizes as fibers and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: keeps in step with them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Entries. A configuration consists of entries. Each entry specifies a fiber and manages it, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the binding runs in both directions: the loader responds to a change in an entry's fields by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjusting the fiber, and a component that revises its own configuration or disables itself has the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change written back to its entry.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • isolate — an isolation annotation applied to the entry's context;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • intercept — an interception annotation applied to the entry's context;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • config — the configuration bound into the component to form its effect function apply;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • disabled — whether the entry is administratively turned off.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An entry can serve as a faithful specification because what supports a fiber is exactly what

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an entry records. The support set of Definition 74 reads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These entries form a configuration tree that is the authoritative record of what the system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loads. An entry may be a leaf mapping to a single fiber, or its component may in turn load

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further components, making the entry a branch node. Cordis provides components for such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (YAML or JSON) and grafts its entries in as a nested subtree. Both are ordinary components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resting on the instantiation primitive of Definition 52 (Algorithm 4), so a nested tree stays

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within the calculus and the results below hold of it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reconciliation. When an entry's record changes, the loader reconciles incrementally rather

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than tearing the fiber down and rebuilding it wholesale. Reconciling this way is sound for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reasons the metatheory supplies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Theorem 80 makes the quiescent state a function of the final configuration alone: what-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever instantiations and retirements the loader performs on the way, and in whatever

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order, the system quiesces where a load of the final configuration from scratch would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have left it. Which components end up loaded is read off the declarations only as far as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each of them installs every key it declares (Definition 76); a component that declares a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: key and installs it under some configurations alone is one the loader can still reconcile,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but the set of loaded components then answers to those configurations as well.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Theorem 73 proves that the system does quiesce, so a reconciliation is complete once its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instantiations and retirements have been issued.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trator to arrange: a fiber whose declared keys are not yet provided waits at its L-Begin, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one whose provider leaves is deactivated ahead of it. A dependency therefore constrains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when a fiber activates rather than when its module is fetched and evaluated, so the loader

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loads modules concurrently, where bringing up a large configuration spends its time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On top of the fiber that an entry declares, the loader dispatches on which of the entry's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fields changed and applies the least disruptive operation for each.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • id, url — rebuilds the entry, since its identity or its component has changed;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • isolate — reassigns the entry's realms (Algorithm 7);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • intercept — updated in place, as interception metadata is consulted at read time and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: needs no reload;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • config — handed to the component, which decides how to apply the new payload,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typically by diffing it against the previous one and reloading only on a material change.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In particular, an @cordisjs/group entry's config is its list of child entries, so it applies the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: update as a keyed diff over child ids, creating, removing, or updating each child; since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: updating a surviving child re-enters this same per-field dispatch, group reconciliation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and entry update recurse together down the tree;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • disabled — unloads the fiber when set and reloads it when cleared.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Managed realms. Isolation in the core derives a child context overriding the realm table ρ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at one key (Section 5.1.2), which suffices while the context tree stands still. An entry may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moved between groups at runtime, so the loader manages realms of its own, and the isolate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: field selects between two scoping rules per key. A value of true selects a local realm, private to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the entry and tagged by its id, which the entry carries with it wherever it moves; a string selects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a global realm shared by every entry naming that string, so moving such an entry changes which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entries it shares a binding with rather than which realm it belongs to. A realm is discarded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: once no entry names it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reassigning an entry's realms turns on which keys changed realm, whether the entry is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provider. The loader answers it with delimiters: one symbol δk per key, under which each context

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.2.2. Hot Module Replacement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hot module replacement (HMR) applies the revertible-effect pattern at the module level: when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: source files change, typically during development, the system replaces the affected modules

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in-place without restarting the process. Because a fiber already bounds all of its component's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects and coeffects, a module that is itself a component can be replaced through fiber opera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions alone: disposing the old fiber recovers everything the component installed, and a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fiber instantiated from the reloaded module reinstalls it. HMR therefore needs no developer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotated acceptance boundaries, as opposed to Webpack [48] or Vite [49] HMR.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The @cordisjs/hmr component provides the HMR engine, which operates in three phases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Phase 1: Module classification. The engine takes two inputs: the stashed set (file URLs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose contents have changed since the last reload) and the externals set (modules that cannot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be hot-replaced and instead trigger a full restart). Writing get_imports(url) for the modules

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that url directly imports, it classifies the changes' dependency subgraph, marking each module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accepted or declined:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Algorithm 8 Module classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 function classify(stashed, externals)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accepted ← stashed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declined ← externals

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pending ←∅

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for url in stashed do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: | pending ← pending ∪(get_imports(url) \ (accepted ∪ declined))

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repeat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: progress ← false

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for url in pending do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: if get_imports(url) ∩ accepted ≠ ∅ then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accepted ← accepted ∪ {url}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pending ← pending \ {url}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: progress ← true

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: else if get_imports(url) ⊆ declined then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declined ← declined ∪ {url}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pending ← pending \ {url}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: progress ← true

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: else

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: | pending ← pending ∪(get_imports(url)\(accepted ∪ declined))

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: until not progress

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declined ← declined ∪ pending

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: return (accepted, declined)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Seeded with the imports of the stashed files, the fixed point accepts a module once one of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its imports is accepted and declines one once all of its imports are declined; any module left

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: undecided, caught in an import cycle, defaults to declined.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Phase 2: Stale-entry detection. Using accepted and declined, the engine then filters the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component entries down to the stale ones, whose dependency tree reaches a changed module. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: walks each entry's tree with get_dependencies, which collects the transitive imports of a module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while respecting declined as a boundary:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Algorithm 9 Stale-entry detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 function get_dependencies(root, declined)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deps ←∅

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: function traverse(url)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: if url ∈ deps or url ∈ declined then return

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deps ← deps ∪ {url}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for child in get_imports(url) do traverse(child)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traverse(root)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: return deps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 9 function detect(entries, accepted, declined)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stale_entries ←∅

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for entry in entries do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tree ← get_dependencies(entry.url, declined)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: if tree ∩ accepted ≠∅ then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accepted ← accepted ∪ tree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stale_entries ← stale_entries ∪ {entry}

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: return stale_entries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An entry is stale exactly when its tree intersects accepted; that tree is then folded into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accepted, so every stale module along it is invalidated in the next phase.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Phase 3: Transactional reload. Finally, the engine reloads the stale entries. It invalidates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the accepted modules' caches³, backing up each removed module to enable rollback, then re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imports each stale entry's component module by its url and swaps in a fresh fiber:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Algorithm 10 Transactional module reload

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 function reload(ctx, accepted, stale_entries)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backup ← invalidate_caches(accepted)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: try

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for entry in stale_entries do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entry.fiber.dispose()

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entry.fiber ← ctx.use(import(entry.url), entry.config)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: catch error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restore_caches(backup)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for entry in stale_entries do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entry.fiber.dispose()

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entry.fiber ← ctx.use(backup[entry.url], entry.config)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: throw error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The transactional guarantee ensures that the system never enters a half-reloaded state: if

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any module fails to import (e.g., due to a syntax error), the caches are restored and every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stale entry is rebuilt from backup[entry.url], the previous component whose cache was just

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restored, undoing the swaps already made.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.3. Case Study: Koishi

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Koishi is an open-source chatbot application framework built on Cordis⁴. Over four years of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development, it has accumulated over 4000 community-contributed plugins³, ranging from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instant-messaging (IM) adapters and database drivers to administrative consoles and end-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: user features. Its scale and diversity make it a representative validation of Cordis's dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composability in a production setting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Expressiveness and generality of the meta-framework. Koishi runs as a server-side bot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose every feature is realized as a plugin over the context primitives of Section 5.1; Koishi

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itself contributes only the chatbot-domain vocabulary. The same model reappears in a wholly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different runtime: Koishi's web console is a second, independent Cordis application whose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plugins compose the primitives of the browser and its user interface rather than those of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: server. The disparate settings above establish two properties of the model of Section 3. (1) It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is expressive: its primitives suffice to carry a complete production system, the host framework

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supplying only domain vocabulary. (2) It is general: it fixes how effects and coeffects compose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while leaving their meaning to each application, and so presupposes neither a particular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain nor a particular runtime.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal composability without cognitive overhead. The plugin systems surveyed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 1.2.1 cannot unload an individual extension's effects without restarting the extension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3On Node.js, this means clearing the caches of both the ES module and CommonJS module systems, since a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module imported through the ES loader can appear in both.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4Koishi currently uses Cordis v3. This paper presents Cordis v4, which refines the effect and coeffect semantics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and redesigns the loader; the core compositional model is shared across both versions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5Koishi uses the term plugin for the concept this paper formalizes as component.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: host. Koishi routinely performs this operation: an orchestrator disables a plugin from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: console and its effects are reverted in place; during development, the HMR engine re-applies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edited plugins on save while preserving cache state and live connections elsewhere in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system. Cordis makes such removal not merely possible but effortless for the plugin author.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Because effects performed through the context are tracked and their inverses composed auto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matically (Section 3.1), even an inexperienced author obtains ordered cleanup for a plugin's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context-mediated effects without writing an uninstall path. This achieves the locality of concern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose absence Section 1.2.1 identifies: correctness that would otherwise rest on each author's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diligence is instead discharged once, by the abstraction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial composability across an open ecosystem. In contrast to the plugin systems of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 1.2.1, where inter-plugin dependencies are largely absent, Koishi's ecosystem exhibits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a genuine dependency topology: IM adapters provide access to each messaging platform,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: database drivers provide persistent storage, and functional plugins declare these as coeffects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and access them. Reconfiguring a provider at runtime, such as switching the storage backend or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconnecting an adapter, reactivates only the dependents whose resolved dependency changed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 3.2); a plugin whose dependency is unavailable stays inactive until it appears, without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erroring. What the case study substantiates is that this composition holds across independently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: authored code: a plugin and its dependencies are typically written by different authors who

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coordinate on nothing beyond the coeffect that connects them, so reactive coeffects keep the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assembly consistent across an open ecosystem of independent contributors.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Threats to validity. The evidence here is drawn from a single ecosystem in a single host lan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guage, so it cannot separate the merits of the paradigm from those of its TypeScript realization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or of Koishi's particular domain, and it is observational rather than a controlled comparison

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against an alternative architecture. What the case study establishes is thus an existence-and-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adoption result rather than a quantitative one; measuring the abstraction's overhead and its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect on developer productivity against a baseline remains future work.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6. Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The formal model and implementation presented in the preceding sections introduce a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: programming paradigm for dynamic composability. This section examines how the paradigm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extends to broader engineering concerns, and discusses the design tensions and open prob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.1. System Boundary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Every effect in Section 3.1 carries an inverse, and what that inverse amounts to is settled by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system boundary. The boundary divides the environment a system runs against into two parts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) A location lies inside when the system is able to modify it exclusively and to restore the state

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: before that modification, so an operation on it is tracked in Γ and can be reverted later. (2) A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: location lies outside when either ability fails, so an operation on it acts as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and is therefore

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neither tracked nor reverted. This section develops the properties of this boundary and their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consequences for recovery.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Boundaries from coeffects. A coeffect moves the boundary by reifying an external location:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it confines every access to that location to a set of operations it provides, each of which it can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supply an inverse for, so operations that acted as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: come to be tracked in Γ and reverted. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundary is therefore drawn per location rather than per medium, since both aforementioned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abilities are properties of a location, and reification changes how a location is accessed while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leaving its medium as it was. For example, a memory region lies inside when the system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alone writes it, and outside when other processes write it too; a file lies inside when only the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system can reach it, as with a scratch file under a private path, and outside when it is a path

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other programs read or write. Moving the boundary is itself a trade-off, between whether the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environment provides revertible semantics for a location and what supplying those semantics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: costs on every access. We take up the co-design this suggests in Section 6.7.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Acquisition and emission. An operation that reaches outside the boundary generally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proceeds in two stages. (1) In the acquisition stage, the operation obtains access and installs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a record inside the boundary: open installs a descriptor that close removes, malloc reserves a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: block that free releases, fork starts a child process that kill terminates. The record itself is part

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the coeffect that reifies the location, e.g. an entry in a map it keeps, and installing that entry

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is a revertible effect. That record is at the same time the channel along which data can leave. (2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the emission stage, the operation pushes data through that channel, as with the bytes a write

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hands to the file or the datagram a send puts on the wire, and the push acts as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , leaving the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data where other parties may read and write it. The two stages therefore fall on opposite sides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the boundary: the acquisition stays inside it, whereas the emission crosses to the outside.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Withholding and compensation. A system that must nonetheless recover from an emission

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has two approaches available. One is to withhold an emission until the state that produced it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is certain to persist, which is the output commit problem of rollback-recovery [50]. The other is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compensation [51]: an action that restores the state up to an equivalence the application supplies,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coarser than the ≈ of Definition 33, as in deleting a file that was created or refunding a charge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that was made. Such actions compose in the same LIFO order as inverses do, so the composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Section 3.1 transfers to them. The metatheory does not: the commutation of Definition 65 is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proved against ≈ and has to be re-established against the coarser one.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.2. Service Multiplexing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dynamic component platforms such as OSGi [52] organize composition around services: units

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of functionality that a provider publishes under an interface and a consumer binds to. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cordis coeffect model echoes this notion, with a service corresponding to the interface behind

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a key. Components that provide a service are its providers, and components that inject a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: service are its consumers. A single service may be implemented by multiple providers, and this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiplicity can be realized in two forms. (1) Exclusive binding: several implementations share

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one interface but at most one is bound at a time; the orchestrator selects which implementation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is bound, and switching between them requires unloading one provider and loading another,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: momentarily perturbing every consumer's dependency. (2) Service broker: a central service

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that acts as the entrypoint for the interface is injected by both the backing providers and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consumers, so that multiple providers coexist and the broker dispatches each request among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them. Compared to exclusive binding, the broker absorbs this perturbation: updating a backing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provider leaves the broker in place, so consumers see no change to their dependency and no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reload is triggered.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The service broker underlies three capabilities: load balancing, rolling updates, and cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process invocation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Load balancing. When several providers coexist, the broker distributes requests among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them according to a configurable policy (e.g., round-robin, least-loaded, latency-weighted) or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an explicit target named by the consumer. Because providers are ordinary components, they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be added or removed to scale capacity up or down; each provider registers with the broker

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through a revertible effect, so unloading it reverts the registration and drops it from the broker's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: routing set automatically.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Rolling updates. Upgrading a service implementation at runtime reduces to a controlled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provider transition [53, 54]. To carry out the transition, the new provider is loaded as an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additional fiber and registers with the broker; once it becomes ACTIVE, traffic is gradually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shifted from the old providers to the new one (e.g., by adjusting selection weights), and the old

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providers are unloaded once they no longer carry in-flight requests. This provider transition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: turns what is traditionally an infrastructure-level operation (e.g., container orchestration, blue-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: green deployment) into an application-level composition pattern.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cross-process invocation. The service broker can also be applied across process boundaries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [55]. Each process hosts its own Cordis context with local providers; a coordinating compo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nent links them, treating each as a remote provider. Cross-process service access is mediated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by an RPC mechanism that preserves the interface, making the distribution transparent to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consumers. One caveat is that a cross-process call incurs latency and may fail mid-flight, so

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposing it synchronously would block the caller. An interface intended to be exposed across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processes must therefore be designed against an asynchronous contract.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.3. Access Control and Sandboxing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given an application assembled from independent components, securing the application calls

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for two complementary mechanisms: (1) constraining what dependencies a component may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: access, and (2) sandboxing untrusted code from the host environment. Cordis supports the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through dependency declarations and interception; the second requires an external sandbox.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Capability-based access control. The dependency access mechanism (Section 5.1.4)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: already constitutes a form of access control over proxy-mediated properties: a component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can only access dependencies it has declared; an undeclared access raises an error. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is structurally similar to capability-based security [56–58], where authority is conferred by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possession of a reference rather than by ambient authority. The inject declaration acts as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capability request, and the context proxy acts as a capability mediator. Since these requests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are declared statically, the complete set of proxy-mediated capabilities a component requires

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is known before it runs, letting the orchestrator review and approve them at load time rather

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than discovering accesses as they happen.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This mediation generalizes to fine-grained policy through the interception mechanism.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Access-control metadata can be carried by contexts or declared by components (Definition 26),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the provider consults it when the dependency is invoked to decide whether a request is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: permitted. For example, a filesystem dependency may carry metadata declaring which paths a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component may read or write, and the provider checks each call against the metadata. Because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this interception lives on the context rather than in either party's code, an orchestrator can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjust it to constrain any component's access to a dependency without modifying the provider,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: granting read-only database access to a community component whereas a core component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retains full access. Moreover, since interception affects only how a dependency is invoked,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not whether it is satisfied, it can be installed, reconfigured, or removed at runtime without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: triggering any reload or perturbing the dependency graph.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Sandboxing untrusted components. When a component's code cannot be trusted, lan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guage-level access control is insufficient, since a malicious component with access to the host

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runtime can reach the underlying objects directly, rendering such checks moot. Sandboxing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires an execution boundary beyond the reach of language-level means, such as software

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fault isolation [59], a separate language runtime, a sandboxed process, or a virtualized con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tainer [60]. Whatever the mechanism, the untrusted component runs in its own sandboxed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context and reaches host-provided dependencies through a bridge, generalizing the cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process invocation of Section 6.2: the same transparency argument renders this bridged access

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indistinguishable from local injection. On the host side, the bridge is an ordinary fiber whose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities can be attenuated by the access control described above.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.4. Language Independence and Selection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although Cordis is implemented in TypeScript, the context paradigm is language-agnostic:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatiotemporal composability is defined only by its two composability dimensions, and thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be realized in any language that meets certain requirements along both. We analyze these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requirements along each dimension in turn.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal composability. At its most basic, temporal composability requires closures: a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revertible effect pairs an action with an inverse, and that inverse must be captured as a value,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along with the state it restores, so it can be replayed on teardown. Beyond this, a component's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: code and the side effects of loading it must be introducible and retractable at runtime.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: How a language meets this second requirement depends on its execution model. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: managed runtimes, this takes the form of a programmatic module registry, where a loaded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module can be evicted from the registry and garbage-collected once unreferenced; Node.js,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for instance, exposes such a registry.6 Native code exposes no module registry, so introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and retraction take the form of explicit dynamic linking and unlinking (e.g., dlopen/dlclose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on Unix, LoadLibrary/FreeLibrary on Windows) [61], i.e., loading object code into a running

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process and later detaching it. WebAssembly takes one path or the other depending on its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedder: a module instance is reclaimed by the host's collector under a managed embedder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., a JavaScript host), or released when a native embedder drops it (e.g., Wasmtime). Across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these mechanisms, the revertible effects model treats loading as an effect on the context, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverses that undo the registration of symbols, types, or handlers the module introduced.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial composability. Spatial composability requires a mechanism for components to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declare their dependencies and for the runtime to provide and inject these dependencies. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduces to a dependency injection (DI) problem [39], which manifests at two levels that differ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across languages: how dependencies are typed and how their access is mediated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At the type level, the language should provide a way for developers to express well-typed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency access. A consumer obtains a coeffect by reading its key from the context, so the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context type (Section 3.2.1) must record each key's coeffect. Typeclasses (Haskell) [62] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traits (Rust) [63] achieve this by letting a provider extend the context type from its own

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module through an instance or impl [64]. TypeScript's module augmentation [65] likewise lets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a provider module merge declarations into the context type.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At the runtime level, dependency access must be dynamically mediated: the coeffect behind

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a key may change as providers are loaded and unloaded, and may be resolved differently across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6CommonJS exposes the module cache via require. cache; ES modules provide no public eviction API, though

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modules can still be managed through engine-internal interfaces.
